I’ll start by checking the Edition 04 baseline against the working manuscripts and Lean packages. Then I’ll assign bounded proof packets for the fixed-source deformation and the mixed presentation, with independent readers checking the exact statements before integration.

The working tree contains a newer surgery manuscript than the Edition 04 baseline. It identifies the meridian-first cut in the Mazur control and accounts for the energy of stretching its band. The matrix normalization now checks in Lean. I’m also working through the round split control, where the two capped metrics can be written down explicitly and their signs tested on the same source.

Lean now derives the vanishing of the entire winding-zero linking block from the integral cokernel of the full outgoing boundary. It also checks the three-to-two count on the original Morse source when a geometric cancelling pair is supplied. On the analytic side, the fixed-source mass theorem is through: it takes the cap infima on the two fixed marked types before making any statement about a minimizing sequence.

The round equator now gives a complete fixed-source example. The two widths can differ, both capped metrics agree with the joined endpoint on their entire retained hemispheres, and both Weyl charges vanish throughout the path. The compact Sobolev estimate also proves positivity of the round Yamabe class, removing the last sign assumption from this example. I’m checking the assembled public statement and the blueprint against those proofs.

The public build passed. Independent replay matched all 1,066 prior declaration records byte for byte and exercised the new round result at unequal widths. The topology readback also confirmed which Mazur cut carries the product metric and which upper map closes the three-to-two successor. I’m recording those distinctions and the remaining obstruction in the handoff.

**Edition 04 reached milestone FOT-E44.** Lean now checks the full exact-face construction on the unit round \(S^4\). For any two independently chosen physical latitude widths in \((0,\pi/2)\), the path preserves the outer metric, reaches a round product near the equator, and gives two positive Yamabe caps that agree with the endpoint on their entire retained hemispheres. Both chiral charges vanish throughout the path, so the strict joined bound holds at every time. [Round construction and independent readback](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/03_single_cut_descent/reviews/ED04_ROUND_FACE_READBACK.md)

**The mass test now applies before any sequence limit.** On a fixed source, arbitrarily accurate positive caps on the two fixed marked closures force equality of the signed raw masses on each side. With the marked reassembly maps and \(e<2T\), the discarded mass is at most \(e-I^+(M)\) in either chirality. This can exclude a proposed cap at a single finite index when the protected disk already carries more than that excess. [Fixed-source proof](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/07_fixed_type_variational_descent/research-progress/handoffs/ED04_FIXED_SOURCE_SIDE_MASSES_20261126.md)

The source readback places the Mazur product band on the meridian-first cut. For the supplied three-middle control, Lean checks the reduction to two given the native geometric cancelling pair, and carries both residual framed tubes and the upper gluing map with its inverse. [Prefix and successor readback](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/10_positive_scalar_intermediate_cuts/reviews/ED04_PREFIX_READBACK.md)

On the analytic route, the corresponding obstruction is the original charged disk without a two-sign saving that covers its protected core and all connectors on the available widths. The round construction settles a standard-type control. Recognition of a further smooth type remains open.

I’ll replay E44 against the current checkout, then follow two objects in parallel: the charged disk with its actual widths and the successor link with its upper gluing map. I’ll track which estimates and markings the sources supply as I test the new proofs.

The opening replay reproduced all 1,255 E44 public declaration records and all installed package pins. On the analytic side, I’ve obtained one volume bound that works for every subwidth and every interpolation time on a supplied compact marked collar. I’m now connecting it to the signed energy measures and checking what it implies for the charged disk at a single finite index.

A new collar derivation supplies an exact round face on the **original E61 disk**. It does so by moving the disk into a small flat region. The outgoing disk then has zero Weyl charge, including on its previously charged core. I’m formalizing the resulting exterior charge increase and checking the cap markings, since that construction answers the face question while leaving the protected-core saving open.

The finite disk calculation now runs in Lean. For either chirality, the exterior gains the original disk charge plus the flattening increment. The proof also bounds the endpoint density against the *incoming* volume when that gain is confined to a narrow strip. The independent topology readback is checking which relative moves extend through the upper gluing and which actually reduce the handle count.

The cap calculation now has the actual round metric in the pocket coordinates. At pocket radius \(b=1/3\), Lean gives metric factors \(36\) at the center and \(9\) at the equator. I’m using that formula to check that one cap metric both agrees with the retained disk and has the claimed signed energy.
